title: Survival, plasma HIV-1 RNA concentrations and drug resistance in HIV-1-infected Haitian adolescents and young adults on antiretrovirals

sections.title: Page 1

summary.text: The opening page and abstract of a 2008 Bulletin study of survival, plasma HIV-1 RNA levels and drug resistance in Haitians aged 13–25 years starting antiretroviral therapy for AIDS at a Port-au-Prince clinic between 2003 and 2005. It sets out the objective, methods, main findings and author and submission details.

sections.title: Page 2

summary.text: Describes the clinical care and follow-up of the Haitian adolescents and young adults on antiretroviral therapy, including clinic assignment by age and pregnancy, visit schedules, management of sexually transmitted infections and adherence support. It also explains laboratory methods, including viral load testing and resistance gene sequencing for specimens above 1000 copies/ml.

sections.title: Page 3

summary.text: Explains how HIV clades, resistance mutations, depression and sensitive social information were assessed and how data were analysed in the Haitian youth cohort. It then begins the results, reporting survival and factors associated with viral suppression at 12 months, such as high adherence and a rise in CD4 count.

sections.title: Page 4

summary.text: Reports drug resistance mutations among 29 sequenced samples from Haitian youth with high viral loads at 12 months, all of clade B, and outcomes for those also treated for tuberculosis. It describes sexual activity, low condom use and pregnancies in the cohort, and suggests that the many mutations seen point to prolonged virological failure.

sections.title: Page 5

summary.text: Discusses how resistance to first-line drugs may leave Haitian adolescents without later treatment options and the public health risk of onward transmission given unprotected sex and pregnancy. It describes a new adolescent HIV clinic in Port-au-Prince offering integrated and psychosocial care and new adherence and safe-sex counselling approaches, and ends with the start of a French abstract.
